question: What are the four primary vital signs measured in routine nursing practice?

options.A: Temperature, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure
options.B: Urine output, pain scale, temperature, and height
options.C: Apex beat, blood pressure, weight, and respiration
options.D: Weight, height, blood sugar, and pulse rate

explanation: These four parameters provide a quick snapshot of cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic function. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: The primary clinical purpose of establishing a baseline vital sign reading is to...

options.A: determine the exact date of hospital discharge
options.B: calculate the exact medication dosage for the patient
options.C: detect future physiological changes and acute deterioration
options.D: diagnose the specific underlying disease process

explanation: Baseline values give the nurse a personal reference point to spot abnormal trends later. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the normal resting pulse rate range for a healthy adult?
explanation: Normal resting adult heart rates fall between 60 and 100 beats per minute. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h2)

question: A weak, barely perceptible peripheral pulse is documented in the patient chart as...
explanation: A thready pulse indicates reduced stroke volume or poor peripheral perfusion. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h2)

question: What is the normal respiratory rate range for a healthy resting adult?
explanation: Healthy resting adults breathe between 12 and 20 times every minute. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why does a nurse count respirations immediately after taking the radial pulse?

options.A: To calculate the correct pulse pressure ratio accurately
options.B: To prevent the patient from consciously altering their breathing pattern
options.C: To ensure the thermometer has finished reading temperature
options.D: To allow the blood pressure cuff to deflate fully

explanation: Patients often change their breathing when they know it is being watched. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: What does the systolic blood pressure reading represent in the cardiovascular cycle?

options.B: The baseline resistance of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: The average pressure throughout the entire cardiac cycle

explanation: Systolic pressure occurs when the heart squeezes blood out into the main arteries. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: Using a blood pressure cuff that is too narrow for an adult arm will result in...

options.C: zero change in the blood pressure values

explanation: A narrow cuff requires excessive pressure to compress the large arm tissue, inflating the reading. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: Where is the normal apex beat of a healthy adult typically located?

options.A: Sixth right intercostal space at the midclavicular line
options.B: Third right intercostal space at the sternal border
options.C: Second left intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Fifth left intercostal space at the midclavicular line

explanation: The left ventricle touches the chest wall precisely at the fifth intercostal space near the midclavicular line. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: An apex beat displaced far to the left of the midclavicular line most commonly indicates...
explanation: An enlarged heart shifts the point of maximal impulse downward and outward. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is a patient asked to roll onto their left side during apex beat palpation?

options.A: To reduce the normal resting heart rate during the exam
options.B: To make it easier to auscultate lung sounds simultaneously
options.C: To bring the left ventricle closer to the chest wall
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing postural dizziness

explanation: Left lateral decubitus positioning moves the heart closer to the ribs for easier palpation. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: What is the approximate normal diameter of a healthy apex beat impulse?

options.B: The entire width of the palm
options.C: The size of a clenched adult fist
options.D: Less than the size of a coin

explanation: A normal point of maximal impulse is localized and typically measures less than two to three centimeters. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: A patient with prolonged, severe hypertension will most likely present with an apex beat that is...

options.A: located higher up in the third intercostal space
options.C: weak, thready, and impossible to locate
options.D: completely normal in size, force, and position

explanation: High blood pressure forces the heart muscle to thicken, creating a stronger and wider impulse. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which physiological response commonly occurs when a patient develops a high fever?

options.A: Decreased blood pressure and slow pulse

explanation: Elevated body temperature speeds up metabolic processes, driving up heart and breathing rates. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: What essential detail must always be included alongside a documented vital sign value?

options.A: The brand name of the medical equipment used
options.B: The full medical diagnosis of the patient
options.C: The name of the pharmacist on duty
options.D: The exact timestamp of the measurement

explanation: Timestamps are mandatory to track physiological trends and medication timing accurately. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: What is the nurse's primary action upon discovering a sudden, severe drop in a patient's blood pressure?

options.A: Ask the patient to get out of bed and walk around the ward
options.B: Document the reading in the chart and take no further action
options.C: Report the finding immediately using structured communication
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled shift change to inform the team

explanation: Acute hypotension indicates potential shock and requires urgent medical notification. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)
